subject: English Language
name: Basic 5 English Language
description: Part 2 of the Basic 5 English Language curriculum covers Grammar Usage, Writing, Writing Conventions, and Extensive Reading. It builds on the oral and reading skills to develop proficiency in written communication and grammatical structure.

strands.title: Grammar Usage at Word and Phrase Levels
strands.description: Developing understanding and usage of various grammatical structures including nouns, determiners, pronouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, idiomatic expressions, conjunctions, modals, and prepositions.

subStrands.title: Nouns
subStrands.description: Using nouns or noun phrases to refer to quantities or units, proper nouns, collective nouns, and abstract nouns.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of different types of nouns in communication

indicators.description: Identify and use nouns or noun phrases to refer to quantities or units

exemplars.description: Introduce quantities and units in context (e.g., a piece of paper, a pair of trousers).
Identify more examples of these in text and use them in sentences.
Make up own noun phrases and use them in sentences.

indicators.description: Identify and use proper nouns, count/non-count, singular/plural nouns

exemplars.description: Introduce proper nouns referring to festivals.
Discuss common nouns, count and non-count nouns with examples.
Discover the difference between regular and irregular plural forms.
Identify plural nouns without plural markers.

indicators.description: Identify and use collective nouns to refer to a group of objects and people

exemplars.description: Teach collective nouns in context (e.g., audience, congregation, flock).
Discuss the meaning of these words in context.
Provide more examples of collective nouns and use them in sentences.

indicators.description: Identify and use abstract nouns to refer to concepts and ideas

exemplars.description: Introduce abstract nouns as names of things that cannot be touched, seen, or felt (e.g., beauty, holiness).
Identify abstract nouns in passages and use them in sentences.

subStrands.title: Determiners
subStrands.description: Using articles, quantifiers, possessive pronouns, demonstratives, and interrogative determiners.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of different types of determiners in communication

indicators.description: Identify and use indefinite and definite articles 'a' and 'an' to refer to a person, animal, event, time or objects in general

exemplars.description: Introduce definite, indefinite, and zero articles using text.
Form sentences using the articles.

indicators.description: Identify and use quantifiers to show qualities

exemplars.description: Introduce quantifiers like each, both, all, numerals, ordinals, some, few/little.
Use the quantifiers in sentences.

indicators.description: Identify and use possessive pronouns to show possession

exemplars.description: Use possessive pronouns like mine, yours, his, hers, theirs in sentences.

indicators.description: Identify and use demonstratives: this/that, these/those

exemplars.description: Identify demonstratives in context and use them in sentences.

indicators.description: Identify and use interrogative determiners e.g. which, whose

exemplars.description: Identify interrogative determiners in a text.
Use interrogative determiners in sentences.

subStrands.title: Pronouns
subStrands.description: Using indefinite and possessive pronouns.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of different types of pronouns in communication

indicators.description: Identify and use indefinite pronouns and possessive pronouns

exemplars.description: Introduce indefinite pronouns (someone, anyone, everything) and possessive pronouns (mine, ours) with examples.
Identify pronouns in a passage and use them in sentences.

subStrands.title: Adjectives
subStrands.description: Using comparative forms of adjectives.

contentStandards.description: Apply the knowledge of adjectives in communication

indicators.description: Use comparative forms of regular and irregular adjectives to make comparisons

exemplars.description: Revise comparative formation (adding 'er').
Introduce irregular adjective comparisons (e.g., good - better, bad - worse).
Use drills for practice.

subStrands.title: Verbs
subStrands.description: Using various verb forms and tenses including simple present, simple past, past continuous, and imperative forms.

contentStandards.description: Apply the knowledge of verbs in communication

indicators.description: Use different types of verbs in sentences

exemplars.description: Identify main and helping verbs (primary and modal auxiliaries) in sentences.

indicators.description: Use appropriate subject-verb agreement

exemplars.description: Use examples to introduce and explain subject-verb agreement.
Complete sentences with missing subjects or verbs.

indicators.description: Use the simple present form of verbs to express needs/preferences and thoughts/ideas

exemplars.description: Introduce simple present form for needs (e.g., I need new clothes) and thoughts (e.g., I think you are right).

indicators.description: Use the simple past form of verbs to express past needs, interest and feeling

exemplars.description: Use simple past form in sentences to express needs, interest, and feelings (e.g., Yesterday, I needed some money).

indicators.description: Use irregular form of the simple past tense of verbs

exemplars.description: Introduce simple past forms of irregular verbs in context (e.g., build - built).
Use irregular verbs in sentences.

indicators.description: Use the past continuous form of verbs

exemplars.description: Use past continuous form to talk about actions going on when a second action took place.
Write sentences using the past continuous form.

indicators.description: Use the imperative forms of verbs to give instructions and directions

exemplars.description: Demonstrate giving instructions and directions (e.g., Switch on the light, Turn right).

subStrands.title: Adverbs
subStrands.description: Using adverbs to express manner.

contentStandards.description: Apply the knowledge of different types of adverbs in communication

indicators.description: Use adverbs to express manner

exemplars.description: Identify adverbs of manner in passages.
Write short paragraphs using adverbs of manner.

subStrands.title: Idiomatic Expressions
subStrands.description: Understanding and using idiomatic expressions appropriately.

contentStandards.description: Understand and use idiomatic expressions appropriately in speech and in writing

indicators.description: Identify, explain and use idiomatic expressions correctly

exemplars.description: Discuss the meaning of idiomatic expressions in context (e.g., take after, pull down).
Use idiomatic expressions in own sentences.

subStrands.title: Conjunctions
subStrands.description: Using conjunctions to link ideas, give reasons, and show results.

contentStandards.description: Apply the knowledge of conjunctions in speech and in writing

indicators.description: Identify and use simple conjunctions - because, since, so, although

exemplars.description: Use conjunctions to give reasons, link contrasting ideas, and show results.
Identify conjunctions in passages and use them to join sentences.

subStrands.title: Modals
subStrands.description: Using modals to express ability, permission, obligation, prediction, and possibility.

contentStandards.description: Apply the knowledge of modals in speech and in writing

indicators.description: Use modals to express a variety of meanings

exemplars.description: Use modals such as can, may, must, shall/will, could, would, might, should, used to, have to/ought to/need to.
Use situations and drills for practice.

subStrands.title: Prepositions
subStrands.description: Using prepositions to convey various meanings like position, direction, time, and purpose.

contentStandards.description: Apply the knowledge of prepositions in oral and written communication

indicators.description: Use prepositions to convey a variety of meanings

exemplars.description: Use prepositions for position, direction, time, purpose, possession, comparison, support or opposition.
Write a short paragraph containing examples of prepositions.

strands.title: Writing
strands.description: Developing writing skills through penmanship, paragraph development, and the writing process.

subStrands.title: Penmanship and Handwriting
subStrands.description: Copying sentences correctly and writing compound sentences.

contentStandards.description: Copy and rewrite sentences correctly

indicators.description: Copy sentences clearly in joint script maintaining legible handwriting

exemplars.description: Copy sentences from the board into exercise books using joint script.

indicators.description: Write compound sentences clearly and correctly

exemplars.description: Search for compound sentences in texts and write them out.
Write parallel simple sentences following identified structures.

subStrands.title: Paragraph Development
subStrands.description: Developing coherent paragraphs with main and supporting ideas.

contentStandards.description: Develop, organise and express ideas cohesively in writing and representing for a variety of purposes, audience and context

indicators.description: Choose appropriate ways and modes of writing and organise facts

exemplars.description: Identify modes of writing (e.g., process, narration, description) in sample texts.
Re-arrange jumbled paragraphs into a coherent piece.

indicators.description: Identify the main idea and minor ideas/supporting details in a paragraph

exemplars.description: Identify topic sentences and supporting details in a model paragraph.
Write own paragraphs on selected topics.

indicators.description: Elaborate on, explain and or justify the main ideas of a paragraph

exemplars.description: Provide details (explanations/examples) to elaborate on a topic sentence.

indicators.description: Use cohesive devices to link ideas in a paragraph

exemplars.description: Identify cohesive devices (e.g., firstly, next, finally) in a paragraph.
Complete paragraphs with appropriate transitional words.

subStrands.title: Writing as a Process
subStrands.description: Applying the writing process including pre-writing, drafting, revising, and publishing.

contentStandards.description: Apply the skills and strategies for idea generation, selection, development, organisation and revision in writing

indicators.description: Select a topic of choice on issues in their community, brainstorm and organise ideas before writing

exemplars.description: Use brainstorming and graphic organizers to generate and organize ideas.

contentStandards.description: Develop and express ideas coherently and cohesively in writing

indicators.description: Develop ideas into a two-paragraph draft

exemplars.description: Draft paragraphs linking ideas within and across paragraphs using cohesive devices.

contentStandards.description: Apply strategies for improving drafts for publishing

indicators.description: Review, and revise the draft by proposing grammar for improvement

exemplars.description: Review drafts for clarity and order of ideas.

indicators.description: Edit/proofread draft, checking capitalisation, usage of punctuation and spelling

exemplars.description: Check for punctuation, capitalization, and spelling errors using checklists.
Peer edit drafts.

indicators.description: Display writing piece for peers to read and publish it in the class magazine

exemplars.description: Publish work in class magazines or on notice boards.

subStrands.title: Narrative Writing
subStrands.description: Writing personal narratives with proper structure.

contentStandards.description: Narrate situations, express feelings and convey point of view about the world/ or fictional world

indicators.description: Create settings, characters and at least one plot in a narrative text

exemplars.description: Write personal narratives using graphic organizers like Time Line and 5 Ws Chart.
Organize details into a writing plan with beginning, middle, and ending.
Revise and edit narratives using checklists.

subStrands.title: Creative/Free Writing
subStrands.description: Writing freely on various topics and creating poems and stories.

contentStandards.description: Create texts

indicators.description: Write freely about topics of choice on national issues and issues from different learning areas

exemplars.description: Select topics, brainstorm, draft, revise, edit, and publish creative pieces.

indicators.description: Write poems and imaginative narrative stories using ideas from poems and imaginative texts read or viewed

exemplars.description: Plan and write imaginative stories and poems using elements of narrative.

subStrands.title: Descriptive Writing
subStrands.description: Using descriptive language and sensory details.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of descriptive words/expressions in writing

indicators.description: Use descriptive words/expressions/sound devices/ figurative language to describe places, personal experiences and events

exemplars.description: Write descriptions using adjectives, figurative language, and sensory details.

subStrands.title: Persuasive/Argumentative Writing
subStrands.description: Supporting opinions and writing arguments.

contentStandards.description: Support an opinion in writing

indicators.description: Write explanations to support opinions

exemplars.description: Take a stand on a motion and write down opinions to support it.

contentStandards.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence

indicators.description: Introduce claims and support them with clear reasons and evidence using credible sources

exemplars.description: Provide reasons and evidence for opinions held on a topic.

indicators.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons

exemplars.description: Discuss appropriate language for arguments.

indicators.description: Establish and maintain a formal style

exemplars.description: Present compositions using the structure of an argumentative piece.

indicators.description: Provide a concluding statement that follows from the arguments presented

exemplars.description: Debate on a topic using the writing process.

subStrands.title: Informative/Expository Writing
subStrands.description: Writing informative texts describing processes and events.

contentStandards.description: Write informative/ expository essays

indicators.description: Write sentences to describe a process of doing something

exemplars.description: Observe picture sequences and write words giving information on an activity.
Compose expository pieces on a domestic activity.

contentStandards.description: Write the event of the day

indicators.description: Write about incidence or events of the day and make radio/TV presentations

exemplars.description: Write news from TV pictures or brainstormed events.
Present news to the class.

subStrands.title: Letter Writing
subStrands.description: Writing informal letters.

contentStandards.description: Write informal letters on given topics

indicators.description: Write to friends about events using appropriate letter formats

exemplars.description: Brainstorm features of friendly letters.
Write letters to imaginary friends.

strands.title: Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage
strands.description: Applying grammar conventions including capitalisation, punctuation, nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, prepositions, conjunctions, and sentence structures.

subStrands.title: Using Capitalisation
subStrands.description: Using capital letters for direct speech and proper nouns.

contentStandards.description: Use capital letters to start the first words in a direct speech

indicators.description: Follow appropriate mechanical convention

exemplars.description: Write formal letters paying attention to capitalisation and punctuation.

indicators.description: Writing of lower case and capital letters

exemplars.description: Write paragraphs about friends.
Edit work checking for capitalisation.

subStrands.title: Using Punctuation
subStrands.description: Using commas and apostrophes.

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of how punctuations are used appropriately in writing

indicators.description: Use punctuations: (the comma) to write an address; (the apostrophe) in contraction

exemplars.description: Introduce and practice using commas in addresses and apostrophes in contractions.
Punctuate sentences correctly.

subStrands.title: Naming Words/Nouns
subStrands.description: Using nouns for quantities, festivals, collective and abstract concepts.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of different types of nouns in communication

indicators.description: Identify and use nouns or noun phrases to refer to quantities or units

exemplars.description: Use quantities and units in context.

indicators.description: Identify and use proper nouns, count/non-count, singular/plural nouns

exemplars.description: Identify and use proper nouns for festivals.
Use count and non-count nouns.
Use regular and irregular plural nouns.
Identify plural nouns without plural markers.

indicators.description: Identify and use collective nouns to refer to a group of objects and people

exemplars.description: Use collective nouns in sentences.

indicators.description: Identify and use abstract nouns to refer to concepts and ideas

exemplars.description: Identify and use abstract nouns in sentences.

subStrands.title: Using Action Words
subStrands.description: Using various verb tenses including simple past, present perfect, and past perfect.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of verbs in everyday language

indicators.description: Differentiate between how the simple past and the present perfect tense forms are used

exemplars.description: Identify and use simple past and present perfect tenses in stories.

indicators.description: Use the simple past verb form to express past needs, feelings and interest

exemplars.description: Write stories using simple past and participle forms.

indicators.description: Use past perfect in speech and in writing

exemplars.description: Write narratives using simple past and past perfect tenses.

indicators.description: Use singular and plural subjects and the verb forms that go with them

exemplars.description: Write essays using various tenses and ensuring subject-verb agreement.

subStrands.title: Using Qualifying Words-Adjectives
subStrands.description: Using comparative forms of adjectives.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of adjectives in speech and in writing

indicators.description: Use comparative forms of regular and irregular adjectives to make comparisons

exemplars.description: Describe family members using positive, comparative, and superlative adjectives.

subStrands.title: Using Adverbs
subStrands.description: Using adverbs to express manner.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the use of adverbs in speech and in writing

indicators.description: Use adverbs to express manner

exemplars.description: Identify adverbs of manner in texts and use them in writing.

subStrands.title: Using Simple Prepositions
subStrands.description: Using prepositions for various meanings.

contentStandards.description: Apply the knowledge of prepositions in oral and written communication

indicators.description: Use prepositions to convey a variety of meanings

exemplars.description: Use prepositions for position, direction, time, purpose, possession, comparison, support or opposition in sentences.

subStrands.title: Using Conjunctions
subStrands.description: Using conjunctions to link ideas.

contentStandards.description: Apply the knowledge of conjunctions in speech and in writing

indicators.description: Identify and use simple conjunctions – because, since, so, although

exemplars.description: Use conjunctions to give reasons, link contrasting ideas, and show results in sentences.

subStrands.title: Using Simple, Compound and Complex Sentences
subStrands.description: Applying grammatical rules to form sentences.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of grammatical rules to form words, phrases and sentences

indicators.description: Identify subjects and predicates in compound sentences

exemplars.description: Identify subjects and verbs in compound sentences.
Write about an event demonstrating understanding of subject and predicate.

indicators.description: Construct compound sentences correctly

exemplars.description: Use coordinators to write compound sentences.
Write a narrative exhibiting knowledge of subject and predicate in compound sentences.

subStrands.title: Spelling
subStrands.description: Spelling words correctly.

contentStandards.description: Spell words correctly

indicators.description: Use phonics knowledge to spell words

exemplars.description: Spell phonically irregular words through games and dictation.
Use spelt words in sentences and fill in blanks.

strands.title: Extensive Reading
strands.description: Building a love and culture of reading.

subStrands.title: Building the Love and Culture of Reading
subStrands.description: Reading widely for pleasure and independent learning.

contentStandards.description: Read widely for pleasure, and to demonstrate independent reading and learning in the literary/content areas

indicators.description: Read a variety of age and level appropriate books and present at least a-three-paragraph summary of each book read

exemplars.description: Read books independently and share stories.
Write a summary of the book read.
Present work to the class for feedback.
